data.body:
Operator decision (2026-08-19) — cross-cutting constraint folded into this epic's S5 line.

Ticket `insectile-modest-martin` (d7b9-ac42) has been CLOSED and its requirement folded directly
into the acceptance criteria of `diamond-flavoured-esok` (RP-03 S5) and `postmodern-tangled-mollusk`
(RP-03 S5 T2), so the constraint travels with the work that can actually violate it.

Why it moved: martin was a standalone guard ticket protecting an ordering invariant in
`reconcile.py` during an extraction that had not yet happened. A guard that lands AFTER the
extraction can only DETECT a break; folded into the tickets performing the extraction, it PREVENTS
one. The failure mode is silent — the repair still runs and still writes correct-looking bytes when
mis-ordered — which is exactly the class of requirement that must not sit in a separate ticket
someone might schedule later.

The constraint in one line: `binding_store.repair_at_write_boundary(...)` must stay AFTER the
under-lock staleness gate (`ensure_selection_current`) and BEFORE the pass's first remote issue
fetch. `reconcile.py` is at 799/800 lines, so S5 must extract along an existing call-graph seam
without raising the cap, and must RE-ANCHOR (never relax) the two boundary tests in
tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_recovery_write_boundary.py. Full text and the inherited
acceptance criteria are in both children's descriptions; the rationale is in ADR 0099.
